global_organization_chain: Summary: wildfire response -> Model I normal allocation -> Poisson and area-scaled extremes -> terrain Tabu placement -> sensitivity/robustness -> budget
Front matter: operational urgency -> four tasks -> literature choices -> complete workflow -> assumptions -> notation
Data interface: fire/geography/equipment sources -> screening -> eastern scope -> Haversine distance -> typed records
Spatial interface: coordinate encoding -> barrier/roaming/wildfire grids -> heat map -> frequency-distance score -> four balanced EOCs
Normal-event decision: worst-distance objective + fleet-count objective -> endurance/range constraints -> four EOCs -> 4+4 active -> 8+8 procured
Extreme-event decision: incident history -> Poisson probabilities -> 2.99431 -> three events -> increasing area -> demand/time/ratio curves -> approximate crossover
Terrain decision: altitude/city classification -> four-neighbor Tabu representation -> linear attenuation -> mountain depth-three map -> Melbourne/Geelong/Cranbourne map
Reliability boundary: four one-sided xi cases -> five-percent random distance disturbance -> 1,000 runs -> 95.7 percent arrival -> malformed time-error warning
Action and reproducibility: strengths/weaknesses -> government budget -> regional totals -> references -> partial Python listing -> missing pipeline preflight

main_argument_chains.claim: Screened coordinates and Haversine distance can provide a common spatial input for raster and route calculations.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Freeze snapshots, CRS, screening, and distance tests before treating spatial inputs as reproducible.

main_argument_chains.claim: Raster frequency and inverse distance can prioritize mobile-EOC candidates, but spatial balance needs a distinct step.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use four EOCs only within the paper's grid and compare the heuristic against facility-location baselines.

main_argument_chains.claim: Worst assignment distance and fleet count can be combined into a conditional normal-event drone decision.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Retain 4+4 active and 8+8 procured only after complete feasibility, scaling, solver, and duty-cycle replay.

main_argument_chains.claim: A Poisson count model can turn an explicit incident history into a decade planning scenario.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat three as an internal scenario until event exposure, fit, nonstationarity, uncertainty, and forecast performance are established.

main_argument_chains.claim: Increasing extreme-fire area can stress the base allocation across fleet, coverage time, and equipment mix.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Retain the nine-times-area crossover as plot-dependent and require raw runs and causal diagnostics.

main_argument_chains.claim: A common four-neighbor search graph can be specialized to mountain and city relay placement.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Do not claim global optimality without the complete objective, Tabu controls, traces, and baselines.

main_argument_chains.claim: Altitude and interference should alter relay range, but the source's linear coefficient is only an asserted placeholder.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Calibrate propagation with consistent units and link budgets before using depth-three or city placement operationally.

main_argument_chains.claim: One-sided factor changes and random distance jitter answer different internal reliability questions.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Retain 95.7 percent only as internal evidence and add global sensitivity, uncertainty, failures, and external outcomes.

main_argument_chains.claim: Regional operational scenarios can organize a stakeholder budget only if model outputs and cost cells reconcile.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use 1.13M, 0.83M, and 0.57M as source totals while rebuilding an auditable lifecycle bill of materials.

main_argument_chains.claim: Partial appendix code can bound reproducibility claims even when it cannot reproduce the main results.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Do not infer execution, optimization, or validation beyond the visible listing.
